internal-v2.v1c-metadata-maintainer-clar.title: Internal V1c image-metadata maintainer clarifications

internal-v2.roi-context.title: Internal V2 image regions of interest
internal-v2.roi-context.summary: Internal V1c represents regions of interest as serialized per-image collections on the image-metadata table; each region originates on exactly one source image, while coordinate axis order, per-region identity, provenance, and cross-image correspondence remain unresolved.

claims.statement: Each internal V2 region of interest originates on exactly one source image and cannot exist without that source-image attachment.
caveats: No physical representation or geometry semantics are asserted.
Linking corresponding or normalized ROIs across simultaneously acquired FFDM, DBT, and synthetic 2D images is a separate future semantic and physical surface.

claims.statement: An internal V1c image row carries a represented region-of-interest count together with serialized coordinate, frame-index, and depth-derivation collections whose lengths agree with that count, and represents no regions of interest as empty collections.
caveats: The three collections are aligned by position only; no per-region identifier is represented.
The public count, coordinate, and frame column description was confirmed against internal V1c, and the internal extraction adds a depth-derivation collection.

claims.statement: Each represented region of interest is a four-element integer rectangle whose first two components are the lower bounds and whose last two are the matching upper bounds, but whether the first axis is the row axis or the column axis is not established for internal V1c and components can fall outside the pixel matrix.
caveats: The public row-first coordinate order is a hypothesis that a pixel-matrix bounds comparison did not confirm for internal V1c, because rectangles consistent with each order occur and some rectangles are consistent with neither.
Negative components occur, so a rectangle is not clipped to the pixel matrix and must be clamped explicitly before cropping.
No coordinate unit, origin, or reference-frame statement is supported beyond integer pixel-matrix indices.
Whether the rectangle approximates an original non-rectangular annotation is not established for internal V1c.

claims.statement: Internal V1c frame-index collections are positionally aligned with the coordinate collection, use zero-based indices, and are represented for rows classified as two-dimensional and synthetic two-dimensional as well as tomosynthesis, so they are not a tomosynthesis-only field.
caveats: The public statement that frame indices are populated only for tomosynthesis rows does not hold for internal V1c.
No inventoried column states a frame count, so no frame-index upper bound is established.
An empty frame collection alongside represented regions means no frame indices are represented, not frame zero.

claims.statement: Internal V1c represents no region-of-interest identifier, annotator, or derivation history, and a region is addressable only by its position within one image row's collections.
caveats: Collection position is a serialization artefact and must not be treated as a durable region identifier.
The depth-derivation flag records that a region's depth information was derived rather than who or what produced the region.

claims.statement: Internal V1c attaches region-of-interest collections to individual image rows and represents no correspondence among regions on separate images of one acquisition group.
caveats: The derived acquisition-group identifier groups image rows and must not be read as a region-of-interest grouping.
Linking corresponding regions across simultaneously acquired full-field, tomosynthesis, and synthetic two-dimensional images remains future work.
This context records the region-of-interest semantic boundary and its internal V1c physical representation, not a complete ROI data dictionary.
The physical representation belongs to the internal V1c image-metadata extraction and is expected to change when image extraction is rerun.

internal-v2.magview-representation-conte.title: Internal V2 MagView wide-table representation
internal-v2.magview-representation-conte.summary: The internal MagView artifact is a finding-oriented but denormalized clinical table that co-locates repeated patient and exam data with findings, interpretations, procedures, pathology, and specimen observations.

claims.statement: The Phase 1 internal clinical artifact is the physical table magview_all_cohorts_PACS_v2_anon.
caveats: The image metadata artifact is not part of this profile binding.

claims.statement: One internal MagView row is a denormalized clinical association rather than one patient, exam, finding, procedure, or diagnosis object.
caveats: Patient- and exam-level attributes repeat at the wider row grain.
Co-location does not establish contemporaneous availability or one-to-one attribution.

claims.statement: A represented accession-plus-finding-number identity can occupy multiple rows while procedure, pathology, putative specimen, or finding-descriptor values differ.
caveats: The tuple is a clinical locator, not a unique physical-row key.
Repeated rows must not be silently deduplicated.

claims.statement: Accession and finding number provide the supported internal clinical finding identity; side is a finding attribute rather than part of that identity, and repeated physical rows may represent the same finding.
caveats: Cross-side reuse or other conflicts for one accession-plus-finding-number identity are data-quality issues rather than distinct supported identities.
The reserved negative finding-number representation is not an ordinary finding identity.

claims.statement: Public structure documentation and internal maintainer knowledge agree that finding number is unique within an exam; source rows that reuse one finding number across conflicting sides are treated as data-quality exceptions.
caveats: Physical rows may still repeat the accession-plus-finding-number identity across procedure or pathology attachments.
Conflicting repeated attributes remain data-quality issues without a supplied repair rule.

claims.statement: A populated linked accession explicitly identifies a co-occurring exam in the same imaging episode, such as paired diagnostic mammography and ultrasound; it never represents a prior or follow-up exam.
caveats: The referenced accession may be absent from the assessed MagView artifact even though the source link is meaningful.
Do not use linked accessions for longitudinal prior-or-subsequent exam search.

claims.statement: The linked-study flag is believed to indicate whether an exam has any linked same-episode study, while linkedaccession_anon supplies the explicit linked accession when populated.
caveats: Do not infer or repair one field solely from the other until the flag semantics are verified.

claims.statement: Repeated patient attributes can differ across time because a patient attribute may change or because of data quality; selecting the most recent value requires an explicit as-of time and must not leak future information into an earlier analysis.
caveats: The catalog does not select a universal latest-row policy.
A task-specific current-value analysis may use the latest value available by its declared as-of time.

claims.statement: Exam-level values should agree across repeated rows for one accession; disagreements are data-quality errors without a known systematic resolution pattern.
caveats: Do not choose a repeated exam value without a declared data-quality rule.

claims.statement: The cancer_outcome_registry_id column is a technical reference to a separate Georgia cancer-registry-derived pathology table and is meaningful only with empi_anon; it is not itself a cancer diagnosis or outcome.
caveats: The separate registry table and its physical relationship are outside the current Phase 1 profile binding.
Registry linkage can identify represented Georgia diagnoses that were not necessarily diagnosed at Emory.
No unique durable physical row key is established.
The table inventory retains unmapped columns whose meanings are not governed by applicable evidence.

internal-v2.magview-pathology-context.title: Internal V2 MagView procedure, pathology, and specimen representation
internal-v2.magview-pathology-context.summary: Procedure-associated descriptor slots, a descriptor-derived row-level pathology severity, specimen characteristics, staging, biomarkers, margins, and nodal observations share the wide finding-oriented table.

claims.statement: Procedure-level information is a reliable internal V2 surface: when one finding has multiple attached procedures, repeated finding rows differ in procedure-level fields such as procedure date and type; no durable procedure identifier or one-to-one pathology attachment is established.
caveats: Finding side and biopsy side can differ and retain distinct roles.
Procedure date and procedure type are supported distinguishing fields, but the available table supplies no durable procedure identifier.

claims.statement: Internal MagView contains columns labeled as specimen, staging, biomarker, margin, and nodal information, but available evidence does not establish that specimen-level representation is present reliably or completely enough for specimen-level operations.
caveats: Do not rely on the specimen number or specimen-associated fields as a complete specimen representation.
No complete durable specimen identity, specimen cardinality, or specimen-collection timestamp is established.

claims.statement: Internal path_severity is a supplied row-level inverse severity group deterministically associated with the unordered represented pathology descriptor set and projected onto the finding/procedure association; one finding tuple can carry more than one severity or attachment state across rows.
caveats: The occurrence is not a supplied reduction across every procedure linked to a finding.
Descriptor slots can be present when severity is absent, so the profile does not prescribe backfilling severity.

claims.statement: Any represented internal pathology severity value 6 is invalid or unexpected and is not a clinical severity category; the governed internal scale is the canonical 0-through-5 vocabulary.
caveats: Exclude or explicitly flag code 6 as invalid data rather than ordering or grouping it clinically.
Null remains the separate unattached-pathology state.

claims.statement: Historical public documentation assigns classic severity code 5 to negative or normal tissue and code 6 to non-breast cancer, while internal maintainer knowledge and descriptor associations establish code 5 as non-breast cancer and code 6 as invalid or unexpected.
caveats: Code 5 is the supported non-breast-cancer category.
Code 6 must not be normalized into any clinical severity category.

claims.statement: The internal MagView table supplies finding-associated path_severity but no side-, exam-, or patient-level pathology-severity aggregate columns.
caveats: Open V2 aggregate bindings must not be copied into this profile.

claims.statement: A downstream exam- or patient-level most-severe reduction is analyst defined: it must declare grouping and attribution and select the minimum represented severity because lower scores are more severe.
caveats: This is not a supplied internal feature, executable workflow, or universal default.
Null and invalid or unexpected code 6 require explicit handling rather than silent ordering.

claims.statement: Both comparison dictionaries label tnmpn as regional-node TNM but attach the primary-tumor code list, while internal tnmpn uses distinct pN-like source tokens.
caveats: The physical occurrence remains mapped as unresolved; no pN code meanings are guessed.
Physical co-location does not establish a unique specimen, procedure, diagnosis, or contemporaneous availability.
The profile records representation and uncertainty rather than an outcome-labeling workflow.

internal-v2.magview-coded-values-context.title: Internal V2 MagView categorical and exceptional-value reconciliation
internal-v2.magview-coded-values-context.summary: Most legacy categorical systems retain V1/V2 meanings, while internal source strings also contain undocumented codes, formatting variants, and unresolved numeric exceptions.

claims.statement: Internal V2 feature codes retain their historical MagView meanings unless a profile-specific claim explicitly supersedes or invalidates a meaning.
caveats: The comparison dictionaries do not establish exhaustive internal domains.
Profile-local vocabularies preserve source tokens rather than normalizing them across releases.

claims.statement: Alphabetic internal MagView codes may be compared after trimming surrounding whitespace and uppercasing; normalization does not assign meanings to otherwise unexplained tokens or split composed strings.
caveats: The original source representation remains part of the physical occurrence.
Delimiter, ordering, repetition, and composition semantics remain field specific and unresolved where documented.

claims.statement: Several internal imaging, recommendation, pathology, and specimen occurrences contain represented source tokens whose meanings or formatting are absent from the comparison dictionaries.
caveats: Unexplained tokens are retained as unresolved rather than guessed or silently normalized.
Composed strings remain opaque because delimiter, ordering, and repetition semantics are not governed.

claims.statement: Finding side and biopsy side both represent left, right, and bilateral codes, but null meaning remains occurrence specific and finding-side and biopsy-side values can differ.
caveats: A null finding-side value is not universally asserted to mean bilateral in internal V2.
A null biopsy-side value must not be filled from finding side.

claims.statement: Several measurement-like internal occurrences contain negative source representations whose sentinel or missing meanings are undocumented.
caveats: Do not interpret an exceptional representation as a physical measurement until its field-specific meaning is validated.
Observed absence is not evidence that a documented code cannot occur.
Schema nullability does not establish clinical missingness semantics.

internal-v2.magview-temporal-context.title: Internal V2 MagView temporal and availability limits
internal-v2.magview-temporal-context.summary: The table exposes confirmed exam- and procedure-occurrence dates plus a provisional pathology-report date; no specimen-collection or universal availability timestamp is supported.

claims.statement: Internal V2 studydate_anon represents exam occurrence time; this profile-specific maintainer interpretation supersedes historical public classic-table wording that described a corresponding field as report-signing time.
caveats: Exam occurrence does not necessarily mean the acquisition time of any particular image.

claims.statement: Internal V2 procdate_anon represents procedure occurrence time; this profile-specific maintainer interpretation supersedes historical public classic-table wording that described a corresponding field as pathology-result time.
caveats: Do not substitute this procedure event time for pathology-report or specimen-collection time.

claims.statement: All internal V2 patient date values are shifted by one consistent patient-specific delta, so absolute dates are not literal while within-patient ordering and time differences remain reliable.
caveats: The shift does not establish event meaning for an otherwise undocumented date-like column.

claims.statement: Internal V2 age_at_study_anon is derived from the consistently shifted patient birth and study dates; ages 90 years or older are top-coded to 89.
caveats: Repeated age values may still contain ordinary data-quality inconsistencies.

claims.statement: Internal V2 pdate_anon is believed to represent pathology-report documentation time, but this interpretation has lower maintainer confidence and the field is rarely used in current internal workflows.
caveats: Retain this occurrence as ambiguous until its meaning is independently confirmed.

claims.statement: The assessed Phase 1 table has date-like exam, procedure, and pathology-report occurrences but no supported specimen-collection time or universal downstream-availability timestamp.
caveats: Undocumented date-like columns remain unmapped rather than promoted to temporal semantics.

claims.statement: Co-location of imaging, procedure, pathology, and specimen fields in the MagView row does not establish that downstream information was available at imaging time.
caveats: Task-specific availability boundaries remain analyst responsibilities.
Different date meanings must remain separate; missingness is not repaired through coalescing.
No date is designated as a universal diagnosis date.

internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context.title: Internal V1c image-metadata representation
internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context.summary: The internal clinical V2 profile is currently paired with an internal V1c image-metadata extraction whose rows describe one extracted DICOM image instance each, carry repeated patient and exam projections and serialized region-of-interest collections, and cover a narrower period and patient set than clinical V2.

claims.statement: One internal V1c image-metadata row represents the attributes of one extracted breast-imaging DICOM image instance, with region-of-interest information serialized inside that row.
caveats: The public description of an image-oriented metadata table was confirmed against the internal V1c artifact rather than assumed.
A row is not a region-of-interest row and is not a file inventory entry.

claims.statement: The internal clinical V2 profile is currently paired with an internal V1c image-metadata extraction that covers a shorter period and a smaller patient set than internal clinical V2.
caveats: The pairing is deliberate and temporary; the profile remains internal V2 and is not renamed to V1c.

claims.statement: A clinical V2 exam with no matching internal V1c image-metadata row lies outside current extraction coverage and is not thereby an exam without images.
caveats: Do not derive an image-availability indicator, a no-image cohort, or an exclusion rule from unmatched exams.

claims.statement: Image extraction for the full internal V2 period is in progress and future metadata is expected to expand or replace this image surface, including adding or expanding modalities such as ultrasound and MRI.
caveats: No column, encoding, table, or coverage record is asserted for a future extraction.

claims.statement: The internal V1c extraction inventories no DICOM instance identifier; the anonymized DICOM file locator distinguishes rows wherever it is represented and is intended to be defined for every extracted image row, while the DICOM series and instance numbers do not distinguish one image row within an accession.
caveats: A file locator is a technical reference and must not be promoted to clinical image identity.
Any release-local row distinctness is scoped to this extraction and does not survive re-extraction.
An observed missing locator is a data-quality defect indicating that the image file is unavailable, not intended optionality.

claims.statement: The rendered-image locator columns and the extraction category and pixel-array enrichment flags are represented only on part of the extraction, and the pixel-array flag represents only its negative state.
caveats: A missing rendered-image locator or enrichment flag is not evidence that image pixel data is absent for that row.
The intended meaning of the extraction category and pixel-array flags is not established.

claims.statement: The represented source DICOM modality values in internal V1c are mammography, ultrasound, and other; the extraction is mammography-centred and every non-mammographic row falls into the residual derived image-type class.
caveats: Represented non-mammographic modality values do not establish systematic ultrasound or MRI image coverage.
A modality value absent from this extraction is not thereby absent from internal clinical V2 or from the imaging archive.

claims.statement: Source DICOM modality, the source DICOM image-type attribute, the pipeline-derived image-type classification, view position, and image laterality are separate internal V1c fields with separate meanings.
caveats: The derived classification only separates mammographic acquisition forms and is not a modality field.
The derived two-dimensional class also covers contrast-enhanced, stereotactic, and post-biopsy acquisitions that are separable only through the source DICOM image-type attribute.
Equivalent source image-type tokens also occur under the residual class, so the classification is not exhaustive.

claims.statement: Internal V1c image laterality is an image attribute: the derived final image laterality represents only left or right, is not represented for a bilateral source laterality, and is not always represented even where a source laterality attribute is.
caveats: Image laterality is not automatically the imaging-finding side or the procedure side.
A missing derived image laterality is not bilateral.
The public description of a laterality correspondence with the clinical side column is a linkage hint, not an equality.

claims.statement: The patient identifier and the accession repeat across internal V1c image rows and remain patient-level and exam-level respectively; acc_anon identifies one exam across EMBED even when a data-quality defect associates that accession with more than one patient identifier.
caveats: Treat the patient identifier as a data-quality consistency check on an accession route rather than an exam-identity component.
A cross-patient accession association is a source defect to flag; it does not split or redefine the accession's exam identity.
Repetition across image rows is physical multiplicity, not clinical multiplicity.

claims.statement: DICOM Burned In Annotation (0028,0301) declares whether the image contains sufficient burned-in annotation to identify the patient and the date the image was acquired; YES and NO are the defined values, and an absent attribute leaves that condition unknown.
caveats: The attribute is a source declaration and is not a verification of the pixel data.
The affirmative state is represented in internal V1c and requires appropriate handling before redistribution or model input.

claims.statement: Internal V1c represents a derived acquisition-group identifier that is nested within one accession, can contain several derived image types and view positions, and does not mix a represented left and right laterality.
caveats: The construction rule for the grouping is not established.
The grouping is not a region-of-interest correspondence representation.
The profile remains internal V2; the paired image metadata is internal V1c and is deliberately and temporarily narrower.
This context describes the current extraction only and asserts nothing about a future image-metadata surface.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Linked accessions identify explicitly linked co-occurring exams in one imaging episode, but no canonical internal episode identity or complete episode construction is established.
caveats: The link can dangle; conflicting values across repeated rows are data-quality errors, and the link must never be interpreted as a prior-or-follow-up exam relationship.
The separate linked-study flag meaning remains unverified.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: The table represents imaging findings through accession-plus-finding-number identity that can occupy multiple physical rows; side is an attribute rather than an identity component.
caveats: The identity is not persistent across accessions and does not uniquely identify a physical row.
Conflicting repeated side values are data-quality errors rather than distinct finding identities.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Procedure-level information is a reliable internal V2 surface, and multiple procedures attached to one finding occupy separate repeated finding rows with differing procedure fields.
caveats: No durable procedure identifier or universal one-to-one pathology attachment is established.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Specimen-labeled columns exist, but specimen-level presence, completeness, reliability, identity, and cardinality are not established for internal V2 operations.
caveats: Do not rely on specimen-level fields for current internal V2 operations.
Specimen number is source scoped and can repeat across rows.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.pathol.summary: The internal occurrence reuses the inverse-severity concept for a descriptor-derived row-level projection; code 5 is non-breast cancer, code 6 is invalid or unexpected, and null is unattached pathology.
caveats: Exclude or explicitly flag code 6 as invalid rather than ordering it clinically.
Do not coerce null into a governed diagnosis group.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.demogr.summary: Internal patient date values use one consistent patient-specific shift, preserving within-patient ordering and time differences while obscuring absolute dates.
caveats: Repeated patient attributes can still vary or contain data-quality errors.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.demogr.summary: Internal age_at_study_anon is derived from consistently shifted birth and study dates, with ages 90 years or older top-coded to 89.
caveats: Repeated values can still contain ordinary data-quality inconsistencies.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: The internal row supplies a deterministic inverse severity associated with its represented descriptor set.
caveats: Descriptor slots can exist without a supplied severity, so the catalog does not prescribe backfilling.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: The physical severity is projected onto each finding/procedure association row; no supplied reduction across all rows linked to one finding is established.
caveats: One finding can carry multiple severity or attachment states across repeated rows.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: No internal side-level pathology-severity aggregate feature is supplied.

internal-v2.pathology.her2_ihc_result.label: HER2 immunohistochemistry result
internal-v2.pathology.her2_ihc_result.definition: Coded HER2 immunohistochemistry score or workflow state for a pathology specimen.
caveats: The vocabulary mixes assay results with workflow and residual-disease states.

internal-v2.pathology.her2_ish_result.label: HER2 in-situ hybridization result
internal-v2.pathology.her2_ish_result.definition: Coded FISH/CISH HER2 result or workflow state for a pathology specimen.
caveats: The vocabulary mixes polarity, copy-number or ratio categories, workflow states, and residual-disease states.

internal-v2.pathology.ki67_result.label: Ki-67 coded result
internal-v2.pathology.ki67_result.definition: Coded Ki-67 result category for a pathology specimen.
caveats: This source field is a mixed coded category, not one scalar percentage.

internal-v2.pathology.extracapsular_exte.label: Extracapsular extension status
internal-v2.pathology.extracapsular_exte.definition: Recorded extracapsular-extension category associated with nodal pathology.
caveats: The dictionary's K code has a semantically incongruent skin-related meaning and remains source specific.

internal-v2.pathology.nodal_evaluation_m.label: Nodal evaluation method
internal-v2.pathology.nodal_evaluation_m.definition: Recorded method used to evaluate lymph-node pathology, including a not-performed state.

internal-v2.pathology.sentinel_nodes_rem.label: Sentinel nodes removed
internal-v2.pathology.sentinel_nodes_rem.definition: Recorded number of sentinel lymph nodes removed.

internal-v2.pathology.nodes_removed.label: Lymph nodes removed
internal-v2.pathology.nodes_removed.definition: Recorded total number of lymph nodes removed.

internal-v2.pathology.nodes_positive.label: Positive lymph nodes
internal-v2.pathology.nodes_positive.definition: Recorded number of positive lymph nodes.

internal-v2.pathology.extensive_intraduc.label: Extensive intraductal component status
internal-v2.pathology.extensive_intraduc.definition: Recorded extensive intraductal component category for a pathology diagnosis.

internal-v2.pathology.isolated_cell_coun.label: Isolated cell count
internal-v2.pathology.isolated_cell_coun.definition: Recorded number of isolated cells in the represented pathology characterization.
caveats: The comparison legend does not establish the isolated cell type.

internal-v2.pathology.largest_deposit_si.label: Largest pathology deposit size
internal-v2.pathology.largest_deposit_si.definition: Recorded size of the largest deposit in the represented pathology characterization, in millimeters.
caveats: The comparison legend does not establish the deposit type or anatomic scope.

internal-v2.image.dicom_file_locator.label: Anonymized DICOM file locator
internal-v2.image.dicom_file_locator.definition: Technical reference to the anonymized DICOM file for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: A file locator is a technical reference and is not clinical image identity.
It is intended to be defined for every extracted image row and is release-local.
An observed missing value means the image file is unavailable and is a data-quality defect.

missing_states.meaning: The intended image file is unavailable because its anonymized DICOM locator is missing
caveats: Treat this as a data-quality defect, not intended optionality.

internal-v2.image.png_render_locator.label: Rendered image locator component
internal-v2.image.png_render_locator.definition: Technical reference component for a rendered raster version of an internal V1c image row.
caveats: Represented on only part of the extraction and not a general rendered-image inventory.
A missing component is not evidence that no rendering exists.
Its relationship to the anonymized DICOM locator is not established.

internal-v2.image.dicom_study_identifier.label: Source DICOM study identifier
internal-v2.image.dicom_study_identifier.definition: Technical study identifier carried on an internal V1c image row.
caveats: This is a short study identifier attribute, not a study instance identifier, and its relationship to the accession is not established.
It does not distinguish one image row.

internal-v2.image.dicom_series_number.label: Source DICOM series number
internal-v2.image.dicom_series_number.definition: Technical series number carried on an internal V1c image row.
caveats: Series and instance numbers together do not distinguish one image row within an accession.

internal-v2.image.dicom_instance_number.label: Source DICOM instance number
internal-v2.image.dicom_instance_number.definition: Technical instance number carried on an internal V1c image row.
caveats: Series and instance numbers together do not distinguish one image row within an accession.

internal-v2.image.acquisition_group_iden.label: Derived acquisition-group identifier
internal-v2.image.acquisition_group_iden.definition: Pipeline-derived identifier grouping internal V1c image rows that the extraction treats as one acquisition group within an accession.
caveats: The construction rule is not established.
A group is nested within one accession, can contain several derived image types and view positions, and does not mix a represented left and right laterality.
It is not a region-of-interest correspondence representation.

internal-v2.image.source_modality.label: Source DICOM image modality
internal-v2.image.source_modality.definition: Modality recorded on the source DICOM instance for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: This image-level modality is separate from the exam-level modality description bound on the clinical table.
It is not the derived mammographic image-type classification.

internal-v2.image.dicom_image_type.label: Source DICOM image-type attribute
internal-v2.image.dicom_image_type.definition: Serialized multi-valued source DICOM image-type attribute for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The value is a serialized sequence of source tokens; its element count varies and empty elements occur.
Token meanings are source-system specific and are not interpreted here.
This attribute, not the derived classification, separates contrast-enhanced, stereotactic, post-biopsy, scout, and screen-save acquisitions.

internal-v2.image.derived_image_type.label: Derived mammographic image-type classification
internal-v2.image.derived_image_type.definition: Pipeline-derived classification of the mammographic acquisition form represented by one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The classification separates mammographic acquisition forms only; every non-mammographic source modality falls into the residual class.
It is not exhaustive: source image-type tokens equivalent to a named class also occur under the residual class.

internal-v2.image.view_position.label: Image view position
internal-v2.image.view_position.definition: Represented mammographic projection or view for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: No view code dictionary is established for internal V1c; represented values include untrimmed, lowercase, and specimen radiography variants, so comparison needs explicit normalization.
The plain view-position attribute and the view code-sequence meaning are separate occurrences and are not reconciled.
View position is separate from image laterality.

internal-v2.image.view_modifier.label: Image view modifier
internal-v2.image.view_modifier.definition: Represented view-modifier meaning applied to one internal V1c image row's projection.
caveats: Represented as a source code meaning rather than a governed internal code list.
Only one modifier occurrence is inventoried; a source sequence may carry more.

internal-v2.image.spot_magnification_fla.label: Derived spot or magnification indicator
internal-v2.image.spot_magnification_fla.definition: Pipeline-derived indicator marking an internal V1c image row as a spot-compression or magnification acquisition.
caveats: Only the affirmative state is represented, and the affirmative state does not occur on tomosynthesis-classified rows.
A missing value is not a negative determination.
The flag does not distinguish spot compression from magnification.

internal-v2.image.source_laterality.label: Source DICOM laterality attribute
internal-v2.image.source_laterality.definition: Laterality recorded on a source DICOM laterality attribute for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Two separate source laterality attributes are inventoried; they sit at different DICOM levels and are not reconciled here.
A bilateral source value is represented and is not resolved into the derived final image laterality.
Image laterality is not the imaging-finding or procedure side.

internal-v2.image.derived_laterality.label: Derived final image laterality
internal-v2.image.derived_laterality.definition: Pipeline-resolved laterality assigned to one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Only left and right are represented; a bilateral source laterality yields no derived value.
It is not always represented even where a source laterality attribute is, and a missing value is not bilateral.
Public documentation describes a correspondence with the clinical side column; that correspondence is a linkage hint, not an equality with finding or procedure side.

internal-v2.image.laterality_derivation_.label: Image-laterality derivation indicator
internal-v2.image.laterality_derivation_.definition: Represented indicator accompanying the derived final image laterality of one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The intended meaning of each represented value is not established; only structural association with the source and derived laterality fields was observed.
The indicator is itself sometimes absent, including on rows whose derived laterality is represented, so it is not a total provenance record.

internal-v2.image.body_part_examined.label: Source body part examined
internal-v2.image.body_part_examined.definition: Body part recorded on the source DICOM instance for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Represented values vary in case and include a bilateral form, so comparison needs explicit normalization.
It does not carry image laterality.

internal-v2.image.presentation_intent.label: Source presentation intent
internal-v2.image.presentation_intent.definition: Whether the source DICOM instance for one internal V1c image row is intended for presentation or for further processing.
caveats: Not represented for tomosynthesis-classified or screen-save classified rows, so presentation intent cannot be assumed for them.
The pixel-handling consequence of each represented value is not established here.

internal-v2.image.photometric_interpreta.label: Source photometric interpretation
internal-v2.image.photometric_interpreta.definition: Represented source DICOM photometric interpretation governing the displayed polarity of one internal V1c image row's pixel data.
caveats: Both represented monochrome values occur, so display polarity must be resolved per image rather than assumed.
The polarity implied by each value is not asserted here and must be resolved against the DICOM standard before rendering.

internal-v2.image.pixel_representation.label: Source pixel representation
internal-v2.image.pixel_representation.definition: Represented source DICOM pixel-representation value for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The signedness implied by the represented value is not asserted here.

internal-v2.image.pixel_matrix_dimension.label: Pixel matrix dimension
internal-v2.image.pixel_matrix_dimension.definition: Size of one axis of the pixel matrix of an internal V1c image row.
caveats: The row and column axes are separate occurrences of this concept and are distinguished by an axis qualifier.
Region-of-interest rectangles are not guaranteed to lie inside these dimensions.

internal-v2.image.pixel_bit_depth.label: Pixel bit-depth attribute
internal-v2.image.pixel_bit_depth.definition: Represented source DICOM bit-depth attribute of an internal V1c image row's pixel data.
caveats: Three separate bit-depth attributes are occurrences of this concept and are distinguished by an attribute qualifier.

internal-v2.image.samples_per_pixel.label: Samples per pixel
internal-v2.image.samples_per_pixel.definition: Represented number of samples per pixel for an internal V1c image row.

internal-v2.image.images_in_acquisition.label: Images in acquisition
internal-v2.image.images_in_acquisition.definition: Represented source DICOM count of images belonging to the acquisition that produced an internal V1c image row.
caveats: This is not a multiframe frame count; no inventoried column states a frame count, so it bounds no region-of-interest frame index.
It is not represented on every row.

internal-v2.image.pixel_spacing.label: Pixel spacing attribute
internal-v2.image.pixel_spacing.definition: Serialized source DICOM pixel-spacing attribute for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The value is a serialized pair; delimiter and unit semantics are not documented in the extraction.
Two separate spacing attributes are occurrences of this concept and are not reconciled with one another.

internal-v2.image.compression_force.label: Compression force
internal-v2.image.compression_force.definition: Represented source DICOM compression force applied for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The unit is not documented in the extraction.

internal-v2.image.body_part_thickness.label: Compressed body part thickness
internal-v2.image.body_part_thickness.definition: Represented source DICOM compressed thickness of the imaged body part for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The unit is not documented in the extraction.

internal-v2.image.tube_voltage_kvp.label: X-ray tube voltage
internal-v2.image.tube_voltage_kvp.definition: Represented source DICOM peak kilovoltage for one internal V1c image row.

internal-v2.image.entrance_dose_mgy.label: Entrance dose in milligray
internal-v2.image.entrance_dose_mgy.definition: Represented source DICOM entrance dose in milligray for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Other represented dose and exposure attributes remain unmapped because their units and internal meaning are not established.

internal-v2.image.device_manufacturer.label: Acquisition device manufacturer
internal-v2.image.device_manufacturer.definition: Represented manufacturer of the device that produced one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Represented values include image-processing and secondary-capture vendors as well as acquisition-system vendors.

internal-v2.image.device_model.label: Acquisition device model
internal-v2.image.device_model.definition: Represented model name of the device that produced one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Represented values include non-mammographic and workstation models.

internal-v2.image.device_software_versio.label: Acquisition device software versions
internal-v2.image.device_software_versio.definition: Serialized represented software versions of the device that produced one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The value is a serialized sequence of vendor-specific component versions and is not parsed here.

internal-v2.image.detector_type.label: Detector type
internal-v2.image.detector_type.definition: Represented source DICOM detector type for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Represented values include film and storage acquisition forms as well as direct digital detection.

internal-v2.image.breast_implant_present.label: Breast implant present attribute
internal-v2.image.breast_implant_present.definition: Represented source DICOM indication of whether a breast implant is present for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: This is an image-level acquisition attribute and is not a clinical implant finding or history.
It is not represented on every row.

internal-v2.image.burned_in_annotation_f.label: Burned-in annotation attribute
internal-v2.image.burned_in_annotation_f.definition: Represented source DICOM declaration of whether one internal V1c image row contains sufficient burned-in annotation to identify the patient and the date the image was acquired.
caveats: The affirmative state is represented and requires appropriate handling before redistribution or model input.
The attribute is a source declaration and is not a verification of the pixel data.
NO does not mean that the image contains no annotation; it means the source does not declare sufficient burned-in annotation to identify the patient and acquisition date.

missing_states.meaning: The source makes no Burned In Annotation declaration; sufficient identifying annotation may or may not be present
caveats: Do not interpret absence as NO.

internal-v2.image.dicom_conversion_type.label: Source conversion type
internal-v2.image.dicom_conversion_type.definition: Represented source DICOM conversion type for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Per-value meanings are not established here; the attribute is used only to show that secondary-capture and screen-save rows occur.

internal-v2.image.extraction_category_fl.label: Extraction category flag
internal-v2.image.extraction_category_fl.definition: Pipeline-assigned extraction category recorded on one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The intended meaning of each represented value is not established, and the non-default value must not be read as evidence that no image exists for that row.
The represented values are strongly associated with the derived image-type classification rather than distributed across it.

internal-v2.image.pixel_array_present_fl.label: Pixel-array determination flag
internal-v2.image.pixel_array_present_fl.definition: Pipeline flag recording a pixel-array determination for one internal V1c image row.
caveats: Only the negative state is represented, so a missing value must not be read as pixel data being present.
Its intended meaning and the pass that produced it are not established.

internal-v2.image.region_of_interest_cou.label: Region-of-interest count on an image
internal-v2.image.region_of_interest_cou.definition: Represented number of regions of interest carried by one internal V1c image row.
caveats: The count describes the row's serialized collections and is not a clinical finding count.
Zero is represented and accompanies empty collections.

internal-v2.roi.coordinate_collection.label: Region-of-interest coordinate collection
internal-v2.roi.coordinate_collection.definition: Serialized collection of four-element integer rectangles, one per region of interest carried by an internal V1c image row.
caveats: Each rectangle is a lower-bound pair followed by the matching upper-bound pair, but whether the first axis is the row axis or the column axis is not established for internal V1c.
Components can be negative or exceed the pixel matrix, so a rectangle must be clamped explicitly before cropping.
The collection is aligned by position with the frame-index and depth-derivation collections; position is not region identity.

missing_states.meaning: No region of interest is represented for the image row
caveats: An empty collection is not evidence that the image was never reviewed or contains no abnormality.

internal-v2.roi.frame_index_collection.label: Region-of-interest frame-index collection
internal-v2.roi.frame_index_collection.definition: Serialized collection of zero-based frame-index lists, one per region of interest carried by an internal V1c image row.
caveats: Aligned by position with the coordinate collection when represented; a region's frame list may hold several non-contiguous indices.
Represented for two-dimensional and synthetic two-dimensional rows as well as tomosynthesis rows, so it is not a tomosynthesis-only field.
No inventoried column states a frame count, so no upper bound is established.

missing_states.representation: empty serialized collection alongside represented regions of interest
missing_states.meaning: No frame indices are represented for the row's regions
caveats: An empty frame collection means absent frame information, not frame zero.

internal-v2.roi.depth_derivation_flag_co.label: Region-of-interest depth-derivation flag collection
internal-v2.roi.depth_derivation_flag_co.definition: Serialized collection of one boolean per region of interest recording whether that region's depth information was derived.
caveats: Its length agrees with the represented region count and with the frame-index collection when frames are represented.
The affirmative state occurs only alongside represented frame indices.
It records that depth information was derived, not who or what produced the region.

clinical.image-region-of-interest.label: Image has region of interest
clinical.image-region-of-interest.attribution: A represented region of interest is attached to one represented image.
attribution_limitations: The relationship does not establish equivalence between an ROI and a clinical finding.
Internal V1c represents no region identifier, so a region is identified only by its position within one image row's collections.
clinical.image-region-of-interest.temporal_qualification: No independent ROI event or availability time is currently asserted.
caveats: The internal V1c physical route is row co-location on the image-metadata table, not a join to a separate region-of-interest table.
Correspondence among regions on separate images of one acquisition group remains future work.

internal-v2.clinical.procedure-pathology.label: Procedure has pathology specimen
internal-v2.clinical.procedure-pathology.attribution: Putative procedure-associated representation of a tissue specimen.
attribution_limitations: Procedure-level information is reliable, but specimen-level presence, completeness, identity, and cardinality remain unresolved.
No unique specimen identifier proves one-to-one attribution.
internal-v2.clinical.procedure-pathology.temporal_qualification: The specimen is downstream of tissue sampling or surgery; specimen-collection time is unsupported.
caveats: The relationship is unresolved and must not be used as a specimen-matching rule.

internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.label: Pathology specimen has descriptor observation
internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.attribution: A pathology descriptor slot may be co-located with a putative specimen association.
attribution_limitations: Slot order and duplicate occurrences do not create clinical weight.
Specimen presence, identity, completeness, reliability, and cardinality are unresolved.
internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.temporal_qualification: Descriptor observations are documented in the downstream pathology context.
caveats: Row co-location does not prove a specimen-to-observation attribution; current operations should not rely on this edge.

internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.label: Pathology specimen supports diagnosis state
internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.attribution: Descriptor observations and characterization co-located with a putative specimen representation support a represented pathology diagnosis state.
attribution_limitations: Specimen presence and attribution are unresolved and must not be required for diagnosis-level use.
A finding can carry several procedure or putative specimen rows with different severity states.
Invalid severity code 6 and unexplained descriptor codes require explicit handling.
internal-v2.clinical.pathology-specimen-.temporal_qualification: Diagnosis documentation is downstream of the imaging finding and procedure.
caveats: No finding-level reduction across all linked rows is supplied.
Current internal operations should not rely on the specimen endpoint of this relationship.

internal-v2.guardrail.absent-image-metad.title: Missing image metadata is not missing imaging
internal-v2.guardrail.absent-image-metad.statement: Do not treat a clinical exam without a matching internal V1c image-metadata row, or an image row without a rendered-image locator or enrichment flag, as evidence that no image exists.
internal-v2.guardrail.absent-image-metad.rationale: The paired image-metadata extraction is internal V1c and covers a narrower period and patient set than internal clinical V2, and its locator and enrichment columns are represented on only part of the extraction.
caveats: An image-availability indicator would need evidence this profile does not supply.

coverage.internal-v2.specimen-collection.subject: time.specimen-collection
coverage.internal-v2.specimen-collection.summary: The assessed internal V2 MagView table contains no supported specimen-collection time binding.
caveats: Do not substitute procedure date, pathology-report date, or an undocumented date-like column.

coverage.internal-v2.downstream-availabi.subject: time.downstream-availability
coverage.internal-v2.downstream-availabi.summary: The assessed internal V2 MagView table contains no supported universal timestamp for downstream information availability.
caveats: Physical co-location must not be treated as contemporaneous availability.

coverage.internal-v2.roi-physical-bindin.subject: internal-v2.roi-context
coverage.internal-v2.roi-physical-bindin.summary: Internal V1c region-of-interest information is now physically cataloged: the count, coordinate, frame-index, and depth-derivation columns live on the image-metadata table, their collections are aligned by position, and the empty-collection representation is recorded; coordinate axis order, per-region identity, and region provenance remain unresolved.
caveats: The image-metadata table is not one row per region of interest.
Cross-image region correspondence is still not represented.

coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side
coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.summary: The internal MagView table has no supplied breast-side pathology-severity aggregate column.
caveats: A downstream reduction remains analyst defined and must preserve attribution and null limitations.

coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam
coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.summary: The internal MagView table has no supplied exam-level pathology-severity aggregate column.
caveats: If an analysis declares an exam grouping, its most-severe reduction uses the minimum represented severity; it is not a supplied feature or default.

coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patient
coverage.internal-v2.pathology-severity-.summary: The internal MagView table has no supplied patient-level pathology-severity result or longitudinal outcome rollup.
caveats: Any patient-level operation must declare grouping, time, multiplicity, and attribution before selecting a minimum severity.

coverage.internal-v2.pathology-code-mean.subject: pathology.diagnosis_code_slot
coverage.internal-v2.pathology-code-mean.summary: Internal MagView represents source-system pathology descriptor codes whose meanings are absent from the comparison dictionaries.
caveats: Preserve unexplained codes without guessing or silently normalizing them.

coverage.internal-v2.outcome-capture.subject: internal-v2.magview-pathology-context
coverage.internal-v2.outcome-capture.summary: The available internal profile evidence does not establish complete outcome capture, outside-system diagnosis capture, or longitudinal follow-up.
caveats: Absence of represented pathology is not proof of disease absence or adequate negative follow-up.

coverage.internal-v2.v1c-roi-coordinate-.subject: internal-v2.roi.coordinate_collection
coverage.internal-v2.v1c-roi-coordinate-.summary: Internal V1c region-of-interest rectangles are four-element integer lower-bound and upper-bound pairs, but which axis comes first is not established and components can fall outside the pixel matrix.
caveats: Resolve the axis order and clamp to the pixel matrix before cropping or rendering a region.

coverage.internal-v2.v1c-image-instance-.subject: image
coverage.internal-v2.v1c-image-instance-.summary: Internal V1c inventories no DICOM instance identifier, so the profile records no clinical image instance identity; the anonymized DICOM file locator is a technical, incomplete, release-local row locator.
caveats: Do not promote a file locator or a DICOM series and instance number pair to clinical image identity.

coverage.internal-v2.v1c-image-modality-.subject: internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context
coverage.internal-v2.v1c-image-modality-.summary: The internal V1c image surface is mammography-centred; represented non-mammographic modality values do not establish systematic ultrasound or MRI image coverage, and full-period extraction is still in progress.
caveats: Absence of a modality from this extraction is not absence from internal clinical V2 or from the imaging archive.
No future modality column, encoding, or table is modelled.

coverage.internal-v2.v1c-dicom-attribute.subject: internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context
coverage.internal-v2.v1c-dicom-attribute.summary: Many inventoried internal V1c DICOM acquisition, dose, detector, collimator, geometry, windowing, icon-image, order-number, patient-age, and time-of-day attributes remain unmapped because their internal meaning and anonymization treatment are not established.
caveats: A recognizable DICOM attribute name is not evidence for an internal interpretation; these columns stay inventoried and unmapped rather than guessed.
